rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a good-quality blastocyst, but it overstates image certainty: the image does not clearly show a prominent tightly packed ICM, cohesive A-grade TE, or obvious active herniation through the zona as confidently as described.

Integrates age, BMI, prior cycle, male factor, endometrium, ovarian response, and lifestyle factors well with embryo quality, though some inferences (e.g., female system presumed intact, alcohol effect magnitude) are stronger than the data support.

The reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with probability estimates tied to embryo quality and patient factors; minor issues include somewhat arbitrary numerical adjustments and overconfidence from morphology alone.

Mostly aligned on SET and avoiding assisted hatching in an already hatching embryo, but recommendations such as ERA after two failures, routine PGT-A consideration at age 28, aspirin, and immunologic/NK testing are not strongly guideline-supported.

Provides clear practical next steps for transfer and contingency planning, including SET, lifestyle advice, and further workup options, though some suggested tests/interventions are more controversial than standard.
